## The public record of the case study {#the-public-record-of-the-case .smaller}

::: {.urlbox}
[doi.org/10.7910/DVN/1HOVTU](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/1HOVTU)<br>[the data and code of the OAs, CC0]{.fs-60}
:::

::: {.urlbox .fragment}
[osf.io/3a8bg](https://osf.io/3a8bg/)<br>[the SCORE project of the paper, with the robustness study at osf.io/38rsh]{.fs-60}
:::

::: {.urlbox .fragment}
[osf.io/2ug8x](https://osf.io/2ug8x/)<br>[the replication in the SCORE replicability study: its preregistration and its final report]{.fs-60}
:::

::: notes
Each of these addresses does a different job. The first is the archive of the original study on the Harvard Dataverse, the data and code of the original authors, released into the public domain, which is why each of you could download the file and reproduce a published number without asking anybody. [advance] The second is the SCORE project of the paper on the OSF, with the component of the robustness study inside it and a sub-component for each analyst, where four of the five published their scripts. [advance] The third is the replication, with the preregistration that fixed its plan and the final report, which lists its deviations from that plan. Because the plan was registered first, nobody can say that the analysis was chosen after its results were known.
:::

## The eight AsPredicted questions {#eight-questions-your-answers-already-mapped .smaller}

::: {.fs-85}
| AsPredicted asks | Your block answers |
|---|---|
| Q1 Have data been collected? | "It's complicated – I already hold them", and what I already know, such as the raw gap of `r fmt_num(curve_ref$b_pp, 2)` points |
| Q2 Main question / hypothesis? | the claim, in your own sentence |
| Q3 Dependent variable? | your **outcome**: a greeting by name |
| Q4 Conditions? | your **comparison group** and your **names** |
| Q5 Analyses? | your **model**, **adjustment**, **test** and **scale**, and your rule for support |
| Q6 Outliers / exclusions? | your **emails counted**, **replies without a code** and **bounced emails** |
| Q7 Sample size? | the emails that your choices leave in: `r min(curve$n)` to `r max(curve$n)` on the curve |
| Q8 Anything else? | your justification, grounded in the causal graph |
:::

::: notes
Each question of AsPredicted maps onto a decision that you have already met, which is why the block in your report is quick to complete. The claim, in your own sentence, is question two, your outcome is the dependent variable, and your comparison group and your names are the conditions. Your model, covariates, test and scale are the analysis, together with your rule for what would count as support, written before you run anything. Your decisions about the emails counted, the uncoded replies and the bounced emails are the exclusions, and they set the sample size, which on the curve runs from three hundred and fifty-seven replies to nine hundred and ninety-one delivered emails. Question one, which AsPredicted handles badly for a reanalysis, you answer directly: the data exist, you hold them, and the block says what you already know about them.
:::
